clusters.name: His stepfather's arrival and his father's remarriage, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time Jonah began secondary school, his stepfather Desmond became a fixture in the home while his father Russell's marriage to Bettina was strained over starting a family. Jonah grew distant from Desmond and relied more on his father for notice, while his own anxiety rose as he made the chess squad and felt out of his depth.

clusters.name: His grandfather's death and the move to a crowded house, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Jonah's grandfather Gordon died in 1991 after years of illness. In the months around his death and the years following, the family moved, Jonah dropped his activities, lived in a cramped rebuilt house, fused with his closest friend Rafe at conservatory, then suffered a wrist injury that ended his playing and fractured that friendship. He spiraled into isolation, getting high and fixing radios, lost and low with no footing. By 1994 he was finding his way again through an exchange abroad and finishing his degree.
clusters.change: The period opened with his grandfather's death in 1991, though the shifts pile up from 1989 onward around the family's move and Jonah's schooling changes. The core was the loss of his grandfather and Jonah's collapse after his wrist injury and Rafe's departure, from which he slowly recovered by 1994.

clusters.name: His relationship with Joelle and the return to therapy, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Jonah was in a relationship for roughly eighteen months starting in 1998. Over that time and after they separated in 1999, his insomnia worsened before performances even as his playing reached its peak. After the split he started therapy with Victor Halloran. The relationship held anxiety and high functioning side by side, then split.

clusters.name: His burnout from performing and his grandmother's final illness, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: In 2001 Jonah began running out of steam for performing and his anxiety rose. By 2002 he had a disastrous audition, moved away from Thornbury, and grew distant from his family. He met Marisol, moved to live with her, then split within the year and sank into deep depression. He returned to Thornbury, avoided his family but leaned on friends, and gradually began to recover through therapy and swimming. His grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer around the same time his performing burned out, and she died in February 2004. Throughout this period Jonah functioned poorly and his anxiety ran high.
clusters.change: The period spans from his burnout in 2001 through his return to stability in early 2004. His grandmother's illness ran alongside his own collapse, and her death marked the settlement of the worst of his depression, though recovery was gradual.

clusters.name: His parents' aging and his cutoff from his mother, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Jonah's grandmother Lorna and grandfather Clifford both died in 2008, marking losses in his extended family. That summer Jonah worked at Alder Creek with Silas and found himself too drained to talk with his mother; when she pushed to visit him, they had a blow-up and he kept the door shut. He then left for nursing school in Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to his mother for roughly a year. His aunt Imogen had a stroke in 2009. His functioning was poor and his anxiety high around his mother throughout.

clusters.name: His marriage to Wren and the strain with her family, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Jonah married Wren in March 2017 and moved into her close-knit family circle. Over the following two years, his anxiety shifted: his job steadied and he felt less strain, yet he also felt a constant push to drive projects forward. By late 2019, around Wren's mother's retirement party at the lake house, the picture became clear: Wren's family operated in fusion, talking all day with nothing hidden; when she was swamped, Jonah overfunctioned to settle her; at family gatherings his sleep collapsed and he felt he did not belong. His anxiety rose and fell with her state, and hers rose and fell with her family's demands.
clusters.change: The period began with his marriage but the strain with Wren's family became visible only in autumn 2019 when events piled up around the retirement gathering. His anxiety about his own projects, his overfunctioning in the relationship, and his failed sleep at her family occasions all emerged together then.
